title: LCR circuits & resonance
examples: What is the formula for the resonant frequency in an LCR circuit?
How does the component values affect the resonance point?
Can you explain what impedance means in this context?

explain.say: Today we are learning about LCR circuits and resonance.
First we look at the components in an LCR circuit.
The total opposition to current is called impedance.
Resonance occurs when the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel.
The resonant frequency is found by setting these reactances equal.
In a real-life radio, resonance selects a specific broadcast frequency.

faq.q: What is impedance in an AC circuit?
faq.a: Impedance is the total effective opposition to alternating current flow. It combines resistance and reactance.
asks: What is the total opposition to current?
How do I calculate the total opposition?

faq.q: How do I find the resonant frequency?
faq.a: You find it by setting the inductive reactance equal to the capacitive reactance. This gives the formula $f0$ equals one divided by two pi times the square root of L times C.
asks: What is the formula for resonance?
When does resonance happen in an LCR circuit?

faq.a: The resistance value does not determine the resonant frequency itself. However, it affects the sharpness of the resonance peak.
asks: How does resistance change the circuit response?

faq.q: What are the units for impedance?
faq.a: Impedance is measured in ohms, just like regular resistance. It represents the total opposition.
asks: What unit do I use for Z?

faq.a: Resonance is used in radio tuners and filters to select or reject specific frequencies. This allows us to isolate signals.
asks: What is the practical use of resonance?
Where do we see resonance in technology?

facts: Impedance (Z) is the total opposition to AC current.
Resonance occurs when inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance.
The resonant frequency formula is $f0$ equals one divided by two pi times the square root of L times C.
The unit for impedance is the ohm.

quiz.say: If $XL$ equals $XC$, what is the circuit at resonance?
quiz.why: When the reactances cancel, the total opposition is lowest, making current flow easiest.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because the resistance component R is still present in the circuit.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because maximum opposition happens when $XL$ and $XC$ are far apart.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because zero current would mean infinite opposition, which is not the case at resonance.

quiz.say: Given L and C, what is the resonant frequency?

options.show: One divided by two pi times the square root of L times C
options.say: One divided by two pi times the square root of L times C

quiz.why: This formula is derived directly from setting $2 ext{pi}fL$ equal to $1 / (2 ext{pi}fC)$.

wrong.0: This mixes the terms incorrectly and does not account for the square root relationship.
wrong.1: This wrongly adds the component values instead of using the product under the root.
wrong.2: This is missing the necessary reciprocal relationship in the formula.

quiz.say: If you increase the capacitance (C), what happens to the resonant frequency?
quiz.why: Since $f0$ is proportional to the inverse of the square root of C, increasing C lowers the frequency.

wrong.0: Changing C only shifts the frequency; it does not necessarily eliminate resonance.
wrong.2: This assumes a direct relationship, but the formula shows an inverse relationship.
wrong.3: The frequency is dependent on the values of L and C, so changing one must change the other.
